slot.brief: Rank five radicals (alkyl, allylic, benzylic with substituent variation) by stability; simple concept with substitution-pattern twist.

stem: Which option gives the correct decreasing order of stability for the following five carbon radicals?

verdicts.working: Resonance stabilizes benzylic and allylic radicals; the para-methoxy group further stabilizes the benzyl radical by donation. Benzyl is more stable than allyl, and greater hyperconjugation stabilizes tert-butyl over isopropyl.

working:
Resonance stabilisation: $p$-methoxybenzyl $>$ benzyl $>$ allyl.
Hyperconjugation stabilisation: tert-butyl $>$ isopropyl.
Overall: $p$-methoxybenzyl $>$ benzyl $>$ allyl $>$ tert-butyl $>$ isopropyl.

Independent check: Resonance stabilizes benzylic and allylic radicals; the para-methoxy group further stabilizes the benzyl radical by donation. Benzyl is more stable than allyl, and greater hyperconjugation stabilizes tert-butyl over isopropyl.
solution:
Resonance stabilization gives $p$-methoxybenzyl $>$ benzyl $>$ allyl; the para-methoxy group further stabilizes the benzylic radical by electron donation.
Hyperconjugation stabilizes the more substituted alkyl radical: tert-butyl $>$ isopropyl.
Hence, the decreasing order is $p$-methoxybenzyl $>$ benzyl $>$ allyl $>$ tert-butyl $>$ isopropyl.
